85	  termMonths: number;
86	  extraDiskGB: number;
87	  plan: { name: string; priceCents: number };
88	  gamePlan: { name: string; priceCents: number; termMonths: number } | null;
89	  dedicatedIp: unknown | null;
90	  /**
91	   * Did the customer actually choose/pay for this IP, vs. a VPS just being
92	   * handed one for free by the `dedicated_ip_default` platform setting? See the
93	   * IP surcharge lines below for why this has to gate the charge alongside
94	   * `dedicatedIp` itself.
95	   */
96	  wantsDedicatedIp: boolean;
97	  /** Paid backup retention tier. A full Server row supplies it; synthetic callers must pass it. */
98	  backupTier: BackupTier;
99	  /**
100	   * The ANNUAL discount FROZEN on this server at sale (`Server.annualDiscountPct`),
101	   * or null on a legacy/monthly/flat row. OPTIONAL so the many synthetic
102	   * `PricedServer` display/quote objects keep compiling; a full Server row supplies
103	   * it automatically. When present it WINS over the live `prices.annualDiscountPct`,
104	   * so an annual VPS / NxCloud / game server renews at exactly the rate it was
105	   * SOLD at even if the admin retunes the setting afterwards; null falls back to
106	   * the live rate, which for every non-annual term is identical maths.
107	   */
108	  annualDiscountPct?: number | null;
109	  /**
110	   * GRANDFATHER PROGRAM (2026-09-17): the plan/game-plan monthly rate FROZEN
111	   * on this server at sale (`Server.grandfatheredRenewalCents`), read here
112	   * INSTEAD OF the live `plan.priceCents` / `gamePlan.priceCents` when
113	   * present. OPTIONAL, same shape as `annualDiscountPct` above — every
114	   * existing synthetic `PricedServer` (wizard previews, tests) keeps
115	   * compiling and keeps pricing off the live catalog rate exactly as
116	   * before; only a real Server row (which supplies it automatically)
117	   * actually grandfathers anything. Null/undefined = price off the live
118	   * plan, which is correct for a legacy pre-program row that was never
119	   * backfilled AND for a free/admin server with no real price to freeze.
120	   */
121	  grandfatheredRenewalCents?: number | null;
122	  /**
123	   * RETENTION OFFER (2026-09-17 field, wired 2026-09-19): the one-time percent
124	   * FROZEN on this server's `pendingRenewalDiscountPercent` when a customer
125	   * accepted the "stay and save" cancel-flow offer (lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts
126	   * claimRetentionOffer). Unlike `grandfatheredRenewalCents` (a permanent
127	   * per-month price override), this discounts exactly ONE upcoming renewal
128	   * charge and the caller is responsible for clearing it back to null once that
129	   * renewal actually commits (see worker/billing.ts commitRenewal and
130	   * lib/actions.ts renewNow) — `renewalCharge` itself only reads it, it never
131	   * decides when the discount has been "used up". OPTIONAL / null = no pending
132	   * discount, which is every server that has never gone through the retention
133	   * flow (and is therefore identical to today's behavior).
134	   */
135	  pendingRenewalDiscountPercent?: number | null;
136	};
137	
138	/**
139	 * The admin-priced inputs a renewal is charged against. Every field is REQUIRED
140	 * deliberately, mirroring how the codebase guards renewal pricing everywhere else
141	 * (`termPromoPercent` is likewise required in lib/proration.ts): a call site that
142	 * builds this object cannot silently forget one and fall back to a stale default.
143	 */
144	export type RenewalPrices = {
145	  ipMonthlyCents: number;
146	  extraDiskPerGbCents: number;
147	  backupPlusCents: number;
148	  /**
149	   * The admin-configured ANNUAL discount (percent), resolved from the
150	   * `annual_discount_percent` setting via `annualDiscountPct()`.
151	   *
152	   * REQUIRED — not optional. A 12-month server renews at
153	   * `vpsTermPriceCents(price, 12, annualDiscountPct)`; if a call site could OMIT
154	   * this it would silently price annual at the shipped default (10%) while the
155	   * owner had set, say, 20% — the rate the customer was shown and charged at order.
156	   * Required turns that into a compile error at every one of the ~8 places that
157	   * build this object, so the annual setting cannot be forgotten on any renewal
158	   * path and `displayed === charged === renewed` holds.
159	   */
160	  annualDiscountPct: number;
161	  /**
162	   * OPTIONAL destination VAT/GST rate (percent) for the customer who owns this
163	   * server, resolved from their billing country (lib/tax.ts taxContextForUser).
164	   * Omitted / 0 => no tax added and `totalCents === netCents`, so every call site
165	   * that does not opt in is byte-for-byte unchanged. A charge site passes the
166	   * OWNER's rate so the wallet debit, the card leg and the invoice all agree; a
167	   * display of the owner's own renewal passes the SAME rate so the figure shown
168	   * equals the figure taken.
169	   */
170	  taxRatePercent?: number;
171	  /**
172	   * CREATOR PARTNER PROGRAM (2026-09-26): the customer's permanent RECURRING
173	   * discount percent (10 if attached to an active partner, 0 otherwise — resolved
174	   * by lib/partner-pricing.ts's `partnerDiscountForRenewal`, which always
175	   * collapses to the recurring tier since a renewal is never anyone's first
176	   * purchase). OPTIONAL, defaulting to 0 — every existing caller that doesn't
177	   * resolve/pass it keeps renewing at exactly today's price, byte-for-byte.
178	   */
179	  partnerDiscountPercent?: number;
180	};

182	export function renewalCharge(
183	  server: PricedServer,
184	  prices: RenewalPrices,
185	): RenewalCharge {
186	  const isGame = !!server.gamePlan;
187	  // The term to renew — the customer's chosen `Server.termMonths` (1 = monthly,
188	  // 12 = annual). A game term is now a per-order choice (Monthly / Annual) just like
189	  // a VPS, so it rides the Server row, not the plan.
190	  //
191	  // VPS/NxCloud terms are always one of the 4 standard `VPS_TERMS`, so we normalise
192	  // through `vpsTerm`. A GAME server, however, may historically carry ANY term the
193	  // plan was configured with (a pre-existing game server was created with
194	  // `termMonths = gamePlan.termMonths`, which the admin can set 1..36). We therefore
195	  // read the game term back RAW (clamped >= 1) rather than through `vpsTerm`, whose
196	  // fallback would collapse a non-standard legacy value (say 3) to monthly and
197	  // change that server's renewal cadence. For the seeded games (all `termMonths: 1`)
198	  // and any new Monthly/Annual order this is identical to the standard path.
199	  const months = isGame ? Math.max(1, Math.round(server.termMonths)) : vpsTerm(server.termMonths).months;
200	  // The annual discount to price the term at: the rate FROZEN on the server at sale,
201	  // falling back to the live setting for legacy/monthly rows. Both halves resolve
202	  // the same number, so an annual sub renews at the sold rate.
203	  const annualPct = server.annualDiscountPct ?? prices.annualDiscountPct;
204	  // Extra root disk is billed EVERY cycle at the current per-GB price. Game plans
205	  // are a flat all-in price and never carry the add-on lines.
206	  const extraDiskMonthlyCents = isGame ? 0 : extraDiskCentsAt(server.extraDiskGB, prices.extraDiskPerGbCents);
207	  const extraDiskCents = extraDiskMonthlyCents * months;
208	  // Paid backup retention (Plus) rides alongside extra disk: billed every cycle at
209	  // the current admin price, and — like every add-on line — NOT carried by a game
210	  // plan (renewalCharge's game branch is flat all-in, so game servers are never
211	  // sold a paid backup tier; see lib/backup-upgrade.ts's game guard).
212	  const backupMonthlyCents = isGame ? 0 : backupTierMonthlyCents(server.backupTier, prices.backupPlusCents);
213	  const backupCents = backupMonthlyCents * months;
214	  // GRANDFATHER PROGRAM: the frozen rate wins over the live catalog price when
215	  // set (see PricedServer.grandfatheredRenewalCents's own doc comment) — this
216	  // is the ONE substitution point for both branches below, so a price rise on
217	  // the live Plan/GamePlan row never touches a server that already has a
218	  // frozen rate, while every other renewal-formula behavior (term math, annual
219	  // discount, add-ons) is completely unchanged.
220	  const grandfatheredPriceCents = server.grandfatheredRenewalCents ?? null;
221	  // A game plan's `priceCents` is its MONTHLY base (every seed is `termMonths: 1`).
222	  // Divide by the plan's own term so an admin plan configured as, say, a 3-month
223	  // bundle still yields a per-month rate; then price the customer's chosen term
224	  // through the SAME formula VPS uses. For a monthly game server this is exactly
225	  // `priceCents`; an ANNUAL game server renews at 12× that, less the annual discount.
226	  const gameMonthlyCents = isGame
227	    ? Math.round((grandfatheredPriceCents ?? server.gamePlan!.priceCents) / Math.max(1, server.gamePlan!.termMonths))
228	    : 0;
229	  // LEGACY GUARD. Game servers sold BEFORE terms existed carry no frozen annual rate
230	  // (`annualDiscountPct == null`) and always renewed at the plan's FLAT `priceCents`,
231	  // with no term discount ever applied. Preserve that exactly so no pre-existing game
232	  // server's renewal moves — only servers sold through the new term-aware flow (which
233	  // always stamps a frozen `annualDiscountPct`) are priced with `termPriceCents`.
234	  //
235	  // GUARD ON isGame FIRST. This value is only USED in the isGame branch below, but a
236	  // bare ternary evaluates it for EVERY server — and a VPS `PricedServer` (e.g. the one
237	  // the deploy wizard builds, `gamePlan: null`, no `annualDiscountPct`) then hits the
238	  // `annualDiscountPct == null` arm and dereferences `server.gamePlan!.priceCents` on a
239	  // null, crashing the whole deploy page with "Cannot read properties of null". Compute
240	  // 0 for non-game so the null is never touched.
241	  const gameTotalCents = !isGame
242	    ? 0
243	    : server.annualDiscountPct == null
244	      ? (grandfatheredPriceCents ?? server.gamePlan!.priceCents)
245	      : termPriceCents(gameMonthlyCents, months, annualPct);
246	  // Bill the IP surcharge only when the server BOTH actually holds a dedicated
247	  // IP AND the customer chose/paid for it (`wantsDedicatedIp`). Requiring
248	  // `dedicatedIp` alone used to mean two very different bugs at different times:
249	  // a NAT-fallback server (paid for an IP, pool was empty, never got one) being
250	  // charged for an IP it never received, and — found 2026-09-15 via a real
251	  // customer's admin profile showing a $2.99 "committed MRR" they never agreed
252	  // to — the opposite case: a VPS granted a dedicated IP for FREE by the
253	  // `dedicated_ip_default` platform setting (see worker/index.ts's provision())
254	  // being silently billed for it anyway on the next renewal. Requiring BOTH
255	  // flags fixes both directions: no charge without the address, no charge
256	  // without genuine customer intent to pay for it.
257	  const dedicatedIpBillable = !!server.dedicatedIp && server.wantsDedicatedIp;
258	  const ipCents = dedicatedIpBillable ? prices.ipMonthlyCents * months : 0;
259	  const preRetentionNetCents = isGame
260	    ? gameTotalCents + ipCents
261	    : vpsTermPriceCents(grandfatheredPriceCents ?? server.plan.priceCents, months, annualPct) +
262	      ipCents +
263	      extraDiskCents +
264	      backupCents;
265	  // RETENTION OFFER: a one-time percent-off THIS renewal only (see
266	  // PricedServer.pendingRenewalDiscountPercent's own doc comment). Applied to
267	  // the WHOLE pre-tax subtotal — plan plus every add-on line — because "50% off
268	  // your next renewal" is a single-event promise about the bill, not about one
269	  // line on it. Clamped 0..100 so a corrupt/out-of-range stored value can never
270	  // produce a negative charge or mint a discount beyond what was ever written
271	  // (claimRetentionOffer only ever writes 50). Applied BEFORE tax, matching
272	  // every other discount on this platform (coupons, promos) — the customer is
273	  // taxed on what they actually pay, not on the list price.
274	  const pendingDiscountPercent = Math.max(0, Math.min(100, server.pendingRenewalDiscountPercent ?? 0));
275	  const retentionDiscountCents =
276	    pendingDiscountPercent > 0 ? Math.round((preRetentionNetCents * pendingDiscountPercent) / 100) : 0;
277	  const afterRetentionCents = preRetentionNetCents - retentionDiscountCents;
278	  // CREATOR PARTNER PROGRAM: the customer's permanent 10%-off-every-renewal rate
279	  // (0 for the overwhelming majority never attached to a partner), applied to
280	  // whatever is left AFTER the one-time retention offer — the two stack rather
281	  // than either double-counting the same dollar or one silently cancelling the
282	  // other. Same clamp discipline as the retention percent above.
283	  const partnerDiscountPercent = Math.max(0, Math.min(100, prices.partnerDiscountPercent ?? 0));
284	  const partnerDiscountCents = partnerDiscountCentsFor(afterRetentionCents, partnerDiscountPercent);
285	  const netCents = afterRetentionCents - partnerDiscountCents;
286	  // VAT/GST on the pre-tax subtotal. Default rate 0 keeps `totalCents === netCents`
287	  // for every caller that does not pass the owner's rate (Finding 1).
288	  const taxRatePercent =
289	    Number.isFinite(prices.taxRatePercent) && (prices.taxRatePercent ?? 0) > 0 ? prices.taxRatePercent! : 0;
290	  const taxCents = Math.round((netCents * taxRatePercent) / 100);
291	  return {
292	    months,
293	    netCents,
294	    taxCents,
295	    taxRatePercent,
296	    totalCents: netCents + taxCents,
297	    extraDiskCents,
298	    extraDiskMonthlyCents,
299	    ipCents,
300	    partnerDiscountCents,
301	    partnerDiscountPercent,
302	    backupCents,
303	    backupMonthlyCents,
304	    retentionDiscountCents,
305	    label: isGame ? server.gamePlan!.name : `${server.plan.name} VPS`,
306	  };
307	}

4	 * SCOPE: this promo is granted on SHARED WEB HOSTING ONLY (owner decision,
5	 * 2026-08-11). The grant is gated by lib/promo-redemption.ts
6	 * `firstMonthFreeAppliesTo` — VPS / Email / Game always bill full. This module
7	 * only models the offer's shape (100%-off-first-term); it does NOT decide which
8	 * products get it. Marketing surfaces must read the redemption gate, not assume
9	 * sitewide.
10	 *
11	 * There is exactly one promo now (owner decision, 2026-08-11): the customer's
12	 * FIRST TERM is free, then the plan renews at its regular price. This replaced
13	 * three contradictory mechanics that used to run at once — a rotating 15–45%
14	 * intro discount, a fictional "20% off 3-year annual billing" band, and a
15	 * homepage annual toggle — which produced three different live prices for the
16	 * same plan and contradicted the homepage pledge that the sign-up price is the
17	 * renewal price. Under first-month-free that pledge is finally TRUE: you sign up
18	 * free and then renew at exactly the price shown ($X/mo).
19	 *
20	 * It is modelled as a 100%-off-first-term discount so every existing call site
21	 * keeps working untouched:
22	 *   - promoPriceCents(regular) => 0            (the first-term charge is $0)
23	 *   - currentPromo(now).discountPercent === 100
24	 * The "regular" (strikethrough) price is the genuine renewal price. Renewal
25	 * paths (worker/billing.ts, worker/product-renewals.ts, lib/renewal-charge.ts)
26	 * bill plan.priceCents unchanged — never the promo price — so displayed ===
27	 * charged both at sign-up ($0) and at renewal ($X).
28	 *
29	 * Add-ons (dedicated IP, extra disk) are billed at full price at order time;
30	 * the promo only touches the plan portion (see lib/order.ts).
31	 *
32	 * Pure & deterministic: every helper takes `now` as a parameter (kept for API
33	 * compatibility even though the single promo is always-on). Nothing here calls
34	 * Date.now() at module load, so it is safe to import anywhere.

37	export type Promo = {
38	  id: string;
39	  /** Full name, e.g. "First month free". */
40	  name: string;
41	  /** Short badge text. */
42	  label: string;
43	  /** Percent off the FIRST-term charge (0–100). 100 = first term free. */
44	  discountPercent: number;
45	  /** True for the first-month-free offer (granted on Shared Hosting only). */
46	  firstMonthFree: boolean;
47	};
48	
49	/**
50	 * The one and only promo: always on, first term free, then renews at the
51	 * regular price. No countdown, no rotation — nothing to expire, so nothing to
52	 * fake a timer on.
53	 */
54	export const FIRST_MONTH_FREE: Promo = {
55	  id: "first-month-free",
56	  name: "First month free",
57	  label: "First month free",
58	  discountPercent: 100,
59	  firstMonthFree: true,
60	};

62	/**
63	 * The active promo for `now`. There is only one, and it is always on, so this
64	 * always returns it. (Kept taking `now` for call-site compatibility.)
65	 */
66	export function currentPromo(_now: Date): Promo {
67	  return FIRST_MONTH_FREE;
68	}

70	/**
71	 * The one discount formula: round(regularCents * (1 - discountPercent/100)).
72	 *
73	 * Split out from `promoPriceCents` so proration can price against the percent a
74	 * server's term was ACTUALLY sold at (Server.termPromoPercent) without inventing
75	 * a fake `Promo` object to carry the number — and, crucially, without a second
76	 * copy of this line. Checkout and proration must round identically or an upgrade
77	 * and its mirror-image downgrade stop cancelling.
78	 */
79	export function discountedCents(regularCents: number, discountPercent: number): number {
80	  return Math.round(regularCents * (1 - discountPercent / 100));
81	}
82	
83	/**
84	 * The genuine first-term price for a regular price under `promo`. This exact
85	 * value is what checkout charges for the first term — display it verbatim. Under
86	 * first-month-free (100% off) this is $0.
87	 */

89	  return discountedCents(regularCents, promo.discountPercent);

97	 * genuinely unrecoverable (lib/proration.ts `resolveTermPromoPercent`). "Assume
98	 * they paid the least we have ever charged" keeps a prorated CREDIT below the
99	 * cash actually collected. Proration prices a DELTA, so at 100% both the upgrade
100	 * charge and the downgrade credit collapse to zero — a revenue concession on an
101	 * unknown-rate row, never a payout.
102	 */

**Prisma models** (`prisma/schema.prisma`):
- `Plan` (line 639) — VPS tier. Fields: `priceCents` (regular monthly price), `introPriceCents`/`introTermMonths` (optional low first-term intro price, added for the grandfather program), `cpuCores`, `ramMB`, `diskGB`, `bandwidthTB`, `storageTier`, `active`, `sortOrder`. **`lib/renewal-charge.ts`** — the single `renewalCharge(server: PricedServer, prices: RenewalPrices): RenewalCharge` function. Order of operations: resolve term months → resolve price (grandfathered override wins over live `plan.priceCents`/`gamePlan.priceCents`) → apply annual-term discount (`termPriceCents`/`vpsTermPriceCents` from `lib/billing-terms.ts`) → add IP/disk/backup add-ons → subtract one-time retention discount → subtract Creator Partner recurring discount (`lib/partner-discount.ts` `partnerDiscountCentsFor`) → add tax. Comment explicitly warns this is the ONE formula (a past incident had a hardcoded duplicate that undercharged).

**`lib/promotions.ts`** — single promo model, `FIRST_MONTH_FREE` (100% off first term), `currentPromo(now)`, `promoPriceCents()`, `discountedCents()`. Scope-gated to shared hosting only via `lib/promo-redemption.ts` `firstMonthFreeAppliesTo("HOSTING")` — VPS/game/email never see it.

**Geo currency display** — `next.config.ts` line 91 confirms `geoip-lite` is in `serverExternalPackages`. Flow: `lib/geo-ip.ts` (`countryFromRequestIp`, wraps geoip-lite) + `lib/geo-currency.ts` (`currencyForCountry`, `countryFromHeaders` — CDN header first, geoip-lite fallback) → `lib/currency-display.ts` `resolveDisplayCurrency()` (server-only; precedence: cookie > CDN/proxy header > geoip-lite IP lookup > admin default Setting). This is DISPLAY ONLY — charge currency is always USD (explicitly documented in the file). I did not find this called from the marketing `/pricing` page itself (that page renders raw USD cents); it's used in dashboard/checkout-adjacent surfaces reading `resolveDisplayCurrency()`.

**Marketing pricing page**: `/opt/nxeon/app/(marketing)/pricing/page.tsx`, exported default `PricingPage()`, `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"`. It queries the DB directly and live on every request — `db.plan.findMany({where:{active:true}})`, `db.hostingPlan.findMany(...)`, `db.emailPlan.findMany(...)`, `db.gamePlan.findMany(...)` — plus live admin settings (`annualDiscountPct()`, `backupPlusMonthlyCents()`, `extraDiskPerGbCents()`) and `planIntroMonthlyCents()` from `lib/intro-pricing.ts`. Nothing on this page is a static config or hardcoded number; a catalog/admin-setting edit propagates immediately. It hands the shaped data to `components/marketing/PricingExplorer.tsx`.

## 2. GAMES CATALOG

**`/opt/nxeon/lib/games.ts`** is the canonical static list: `GAME_FAMILIES` (const array, line 2) has **52 entries**; `GAME_DISPLAY` (line 19) maps each to `{name, glyph}`. Only 47 of the 52 families currently have an active `GamePlan` row (live DB count above); the marketing pricing page filters with `GAME_FAMILIES.filter(f => byGame.get(f)?.length > 0)` so unseeded families don't render.
- Pricing/tiers per game: **separate `GamePlan` model**, not reuse of `Plan` directly — each `GamePlan` references a `basePlanId` (FK into `Plan`) purely to size/provision the underlying VM, but price/RAM/disk/slots live on `GamePlan` itself.

## 3. REGIONS / NODES

**`Node` model** (`prisma/schema.prisma` line 1486): `region` (plain string, validated in code not DB — `lib/node-regions.ts`), `provider` (enum `NodeProvider`: OVH/HETZNER), `capacityRamMB`, `enabled`, `acceptsProvisions` (admin-only "stop landing new work here" toggle, distinct from `enabled`), `status` (NodeStatus enum).
- `lib/node-regions.ts`: `NODE_REGIONS` lists *possible* datacenter codes per provider (OVH: sgp1/bhs1/gra1/rbx1/waw1; Hetzner: fsn1/nbg1/hel1/ash1/hil1) — these are not all live, just valid.

It reads a live list of *enabled Nodes* (so a region with zero nodes, or one whose only node was disabled, simply won't appear) — that part is real and live. It does NOT check per-node capacity/utilization or `acceptsProvisions` before offering a region; those are enforced later, server-side, by the actual provisioning scheduler (worker), not surfaced to the customer as a stock/availability signal.

## 3. REGIONS / NODES

**`Node` model** (`prisma/schema.prisma` line 1486): `region` (plain string, validated in code not DB — `lib/node-regions.ts`), `provider` (enum `NodeProvider`: OVH/HETZNER), `capacityRamMB`, `enabled`, `acceptsProvisions` (admin-only "stop landing new work here" toggle, distinct from `enabled`), `status` (NodeStatus enum).
- `lib/node-regions.ts`: `NODE_REGIONS` lists *possible* datacenter codes per provider (OVH: sgp1/bhs1/gra1/rbx1/waw1; Hetzner: fsn1/nbg1/hel1/ash1/hil1) — these are not all live, just valid.
- **Live DB reality** (queried directly): 4 `Node` rows exist — `primary`/`node-3`/`node-4` in `sgp1` (OVH) and `node-2` in `fsn1` (Hetzner). **2 distinct live regions.**
- Capacity/stock: `lib/node-capacity.ts` computes per-node utilization (CPU/RAM/DISK, `nodeThresholds()`, `NODE_CAP_DEFAULT_WARN/CRIT`) but this is an **admin-only** alerting surface (`/admin/infrastructure`, `NodeAlert` model) — it is NOT exposed to the marketing site or the deploy wizard. There is no customer-facing "X slots left in this region" or "sold out" concept anywhere (confirmed via grep across marketing/dashboard-deploy — no hits).

**Deploy wizard region picker** (`app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx` line 131): `db.node.findMany({where:{enabled:true}}, select: {id, region})` — queried live, per-request, dynamic. Passed to `lib/nx/catalog.ts` `regionsFrom(nodes)` (line 77), which groups by region and only offers a region if it has coordinates defined (`COORDS[region]`) — filters on `enabled` only, NOT `acceptsProvisions` and NOT capacity. `defaultRegionKey()` (line 128) picks the visitor's nearest region (EU visitor → Europe region if one exists, else `sgp1`, else first).

**Answer to "does checkout read live availability before letting someone pick a region/plan"**: Partially. It reads a live list of *enabled Nodes* (so a region with zero nodes, or one whose only node was disabled, simply won't appear) — that part is real and live. It does NOT check per-node capacity/utilization or `acceptsProvisions` before offering a region; those are enforced later, server-side, by the actual provisioning scheduler (worker), not surfaced to the customer as a stock/availability signal.
